title: SC-300 Domain 3 questions (3.1, 3.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Microsoft.

questions.stem: Contoso runs a web app in Azure App Service that must read secrets from Azure Key Vault. The security team wants no credentials stored in code or configuration and no secret rotation to manage. Which identity should the app use?
choices: A managed identity
A service principal with a client secret
A dedicated cloud-only user account
A group managed service account
questions.answer: A managed identity
questions.explanation: A managed identity gives an Azure-hosted workload a Microsoft Entra identity whose credentials Azure creates and rotates, so nothing is stored in code. A service principal with a client secret still leaves a secret to store and rotate.

questions.stem: Fabrikam has a build server in its on-premises datacenter (not connected to Azure Arc) that must deploy resources to an Azure subscription. Which identity type is BEST suited for this workload?
choices: A system-assigned managed identity enabled on the build server's operating system
A service principal from an app registration that uses a certificate
A user-assigned managed identity attached to a virtual machine in the build subscription
A shared user account excluded from MFA
questions.answer: A service principal from an app registration that uses a certificate
questions.explanation: Managed identities are available only to Azure resources (or Arc-enabled servers), so an on-premises server not in Azure needs an app registration's service principal, ideally authenticating with a certificate. A shared user account excluded from MFA is a weak, non-auditable choice for automation.

questions.stem: A Windows service on several on-premises domain-joined servers must authenticate to an on-premises SQL Server by using Active Directory credentials. Administrators do not want to manage the service account password. Which identity should you use?
choices: A system-assigned managed identity
A Microsoft Entra service principal
A group managed service account
A standard Active Directory user account
questions.answer: A group managed service account
questions.explanation: A group managed service account (gMSA) is an Active Directory account whose password the domain manages automatically and that several servers can share. A system-assigned managed identity is a Microsoft Entra identity for Azure resources and cannot authenticate to on-premises Active Directory services.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes how a managed identity is represented in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: As a user account with a password that never expires and cannot be reset
As an app registration that the administrator must give a client secret
As a guest account linked to the Azure subscription
As a special type of service principal whose credentials Azure manages
questions.answer: As a special type of service principal whose credentials Azure manages
questions.explanation: Each managed identity is backed by a service principal in the tenant, and Azure handles its credentials automatically. It is not an app registration that needs a secret, and it is not a user or guest account.

questions.stem: Tailspin Toys wants an automation script that runs in an Azure Automation account to update resources in the same subscription. The script must not use stored credentials. What should the administrator configure?
choices: Enable a managed identity on the Automation account and grant it an Azure role
Create a cloud-only user account and store its password as an Automation credential
Create an app registration and store its client secret as an Automation variable
Run the runbook under the administrator's own signed-in account
questions.answer: Enable a managed identity on the Automation account and grant it an Azure role
questions.explanation: Azure Automation supports managed identities, so the runbook can request tokens without any stored secret once the identity has the right Azure role. Storing a user password or client secret in the account still leaves a credential to protect and rotate.

questions.stem: An administrator is comparing identity options for a new containerized app in Azure Kubernetes Service that calls Azure Storage. Which consideration favors a managed identity over a service principal with a secret?
choices: A managed identity can be used from any cloud provider without federation
Azure issues and rotates the credential, so no secret is stored
A managed identity bypasses Azure RBAC checks on storage
A managed identity works without any token from Microsoft Entra ID
questions.answer: Azure issues and rotates the credential, so no secret is stored
questions.explanation: The main benefit of a managed identity is that Azure handles the credential lifecycle, so no secret is stored or expires. It still receives a Microsoft Entra token and is still subject to Azure RBAC, and it is not usable from other clouds on its own.

questions.stem: A company plans to use workload identities for dozens of Azure resources. Which identity type should the company AVOID for unattended workloads because it is designed for people and is subject to interactive sign-in controls such as MFA?
choices: A system-assigned managed identity
A user-assigned managed identity
A user account
A service principal
questions.answer: A user account
questions.explanation: User accounts represent people and are affected by MFA, password changes and interactive Conditional Access, which makes them a poor fit for unattended automation. Managed identities and service principals are the intended identities for workloads.

questions.stem: Which statement about a system-assigned managed identity is correct?
choices: It can be shared by several virtual machines at the same time
It is created as a standalone Azure resource in a resource group
It keeps its role assignments after its resource is deleted and re-created
It is deleted automatically when its Azure resource is deleted
questions.answer: It is deleted automatically when its Azure resource is deleted
questions.explanation: A system-assigned identity shares the lifecycle of its resource: it is created when enabled on the resource and removed when the resource is deleted. Sharing one identity across resources and existing as a standalone resource are traits of a user-assigned identity.

questions.stem: Adatum runs a scale set whose instances are frequently deleted and re-created. Each new instance must immediately access the same storage account without new role assignments. Which identity should you use?
choices: A user-assigned managed identity attached to the scale set
A system-assigned managed identity on each instance
A separate service principal for each instance
A group managed service account
questions.answer: A user-assigned managed identity attached to the scale set
questions.explanation: A user-assigned managed identity has its own lifecycle, so its role assignment survives when instances are replaced and can be attached to many resources. A system-assigned identity is tied to one resource, so replacement means a new identity and new role assignments.

questions.stem: A virtual machine already has a system-assigned managed identity. A developer asks whether the same virtual machine can also use user-assigned managed identities. What should you tell the developer?
choices: No, a resource can have only one managed identity of any type
Yes, it can also have one or more user-assigned identities
Yes, but only after the system-assigned identity is disabled
No, user-assigned identities are supported only on App Service
questions.answer: Yes, it can also have one or more user-assigned identities
questions.explanation: Azure resources that support managed identities can have one system-assigned identity and multiple user-assigned identities at the same time. There is no need to disable the system-assigned identity first.

questions.stem: Contoso wants to pre-create an identity, grant it access to a Key Vault, and only later deploy the virtual machines that will use it. Which option supports this sequence?
choices: Enable a system-assigned managed identity before the virtual machine exists
Create a guest account and convert it to a managed identity
Create a user-assigned managed identity first and attach it during deployment
Register an app and convert its service principal into a system-assigned identity
questions.answer: Create a user-assigned managed identity first and attach it during deployment
questions.explanation: Because a user-assigned identity is an independent Azure resource, it can be created and granted roles before the workload exists. A system-assigned identity cannot exist until its resource exists.

questions.stem: A team wants each of its function apps to have a separate identity so that removing an app automatically removes its access, with the least administrative effort. Which identity should the team use?
choices: A single user-assigned managed identity shared by all function apps
A service principal per function app with a client secret
A dedicated user account per function app
A system-assigned managed identity on each function app
questions.answer: A system-assigned managed identity on each function app
questions.explanation: A system-assigned identity is unique to its resource and is cleaned up with it, so access disappears when the app is deleted without extra work. A shared user-assigned identity would leave the identity and its access in place after an app is removed.

questions.stem: An administrator deletes a virtual machine that had a user-assigned managed identity attached. What happens to the user-assigned managed identity?
choices: It remains, with its role assignments, until someone deletes it
It is deleted together with the virtual machine
It is converted into a system-assigned identity on another resource
It is disabled and its role assignments are removed automatically
questions.answer: It remains, with its role assignments, until someone deletes it
questions.explanation: A user-assigned identity has an independent lifecycle, so deleting a resource only detaches it. The identity and its role assignments stay until an administrator deletes the identity itself.

questions.stem: An administrator must create user-assigned managed identities in a resource group without receiving any other permissions. Which Azure built-in role should be assigned, following least privilege?
choices: Managed Identity Operator
Managed Identity Contributor
Contributor
Owner
questions.answer: Managed Identity Contributor
questions.explanation: Managed Identity Contributor can create, read, update and delete user-assigned identities. Managed Identity Operator can only read and assign existing identities, and Contributor or Owner grant far more than needed.

questions.stem: A deployment engineer can modify virtual machines but receives an error when attaching an existing user-assigned managed identity to a virtual machine. Which additional Azure role should the engineer have on the identity, following least privilege?
choices: Managed Identity Contributor
User Access Administrator
Managed Identity Operator
Owner
questions.answer: Managed Identity Operator
questions.explanation: Assigning a user-assigned identity to a resource needs the assign action on the identity, which Managed Identity Operator provides without the right to create or delete identities. Managed Identity Contributor adds create and delete rights that are not needed here.

questions.stem: You enable a system-assigned managed identity on an existing Azure virtual machine. What is created in Microsoft Entra ID as a result?
choices: A user account with the same name as the virtual machine
An app registration with a client secret
A security group that contains the virtual machine
A service principal tied to the virtual machine's lifecycle
questions.answer: A service principal tied to the virtual machine's lifecycle
questions.explanation: Enabling a system-assigned identity makes Azure create a service principal for that resource in the trusted tenant. No user account, client secret or group is created.

questions.stem: A user-assigned managed identity is attached to an App Service app that also has a system-assigned identity. When the app requests a token, how does it make sure it uses the user-assigned identity?
choices: It specifies the identity's client ID or resource ID in the token request
It signs in with the identity's password from Key Vault
It disables the system-assigned identity before every token request it sends
It uses the tenant's default app registration
questions.answer: It specifies the identity's client ID or resource ID in the token request
questions.explanation: When more than one identity is available, the code chooses the user-assigned identity by passing its client ID, object ID or resource ID in the token request. Managed identities have no password to retrieve.

questions.stem: Which endpoint does code on an Azure virtual machine call to obtain a token for its managed identity?
choices: The tenant's federation metadata endpoint
The Azure Instance Metadata Service endpoint on the virtual machine
The Microsoft Graph invitation endpoint
The SCIM endpoint of the target resource
questions.answer: The Azure Instance Metadata Service endpoint on the virtual machine
questions.explanation: On virtual machines, the managed identity token is requested from the local Azure Instance Metadata Service, which is reachable only from inside the machine. The federation metadata and SCIM endpoints serve other purposes.

questions.stem: Fabrikam transfers an Azure subscription to a different Microsoft Entra tenant. Virtual machines in the subscription used managed identities. What should the administrators expect?
choices: The managed identities move automatically with all their role assignments
The managed identities are converted into guest users in the new tenant
They must be re-created or re-enabled, and access granted again
The managed identities keep working in the old tenant only
questions.answer: They must be re-created or re-enabled, and access granted again
questions.explanation: Managed identities belong to the tenant that trusts the subscription, so after a directory transfer they break and must be re-created (user-assigned) or disabled and re-enabled (system-assigned), and role assignments must be redone. They are not converted to guests.

questions.stem: An administrator wants an on-premises Windows server to use a managed identity to access Azure Key Vault. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Enable a system-assigned identity in Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
Install the Application Proxy connector on the server
Create a group managed service account for the server
Onboard the server to Azure Arc
questions.answer: Onboard the server to Azure Arc
questions.explanation: Servers outside Azure get a system-assigned managed identity after they are connected to Azure Arc. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and the Application Proxy connector do not create managed identities.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: A managed identity on a virtual machine must read blobs in one storage account and nothing else. Which Azure role assignment BEST meets the requirement following least privilege?
choices: Storage Blob Data Reader scoped to the storage account
Reader scoped to the subscription
Storage Account Contributor scoped to the storage account
Contributor scoped to the resource group that holds the storage account
questions.answer: Storage Blob Data Reader scoped to the storage account
questions.explanation: Storage Blob Data Reader grants read access to blob data, and scoping it to the storage account limits it to that account. Reader covers only management-plane metadata, not blob data, and the contributor roles grant more than read.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: An App Service app's managed identity must read secrets from a Key Vault that uses the Azure RBAC permission model. Which role should you assign to the identity?
choices: Key Vault Contributor
Key Vault Secrets User
Key Vault Reader
Key Vault Crypto User
questions.answer: Key Vault Secrets User
questions.explanation: Key Vault Secrets User lets a principal read secret contents in a vault that uses the Azure RBAC permission model. Key Vault Contributor manages the vault itself but does not grant data access, and Key Vault Reader reads metadata only.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: An administrator must assign an Azure role to a managed identity on a storage account. Which role does the administrator need, following least privilege?
choices: Contributor
Managed Identity Operator
Role Based Access Control Administrator
Global Administrator
questions.answer: Role Based Access Control Administrator
questions.explanation: Creating Azure role assignments requires the role assignment write permission, which Role Based Access Control Administrator provides without other management rights (Owner and User Access Administrator also have it). Contributor cannot create role assignments, and Managed Identity Operator only assigns identities to resources.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: A function app's managed identity was granted a role on a storage account, but requests still fail. Which issue is MOST likely if the role was granted only a few minutes ago?
choices: Managed identities cannot be assigned data-plane roles
The managed identity must first be added as a guest user
The storage account must be moved to the function app's resource group
Role assignment changes and cached tokens can take time to take effect
questions.answer: Role assignment changes and cached tokens can take time to take effect
questions.explanation: Azure role assignments can take a while to propagate, and a token issued before the change does not reflect it until it is refreshed. Managed identities can hold data-plane roles, and the resources do not need to share a resource group.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: Contoso wants a single user-assigned managed identity used by several virtual machines to read secrets from three Key Vaults in one resource group, and no others. Where should the role assignment be scoped to meet the requirement with the LEAST administrative effort?
choices: The resource group that contains the three Key Vaults
Each virtual machine
The management group above the subscription
The Microsoft Entra tenant root
questions.answer: The resource group that contains the three Key Vaults
questions.explanation: Scoping one assignment to the resource group covers all three vaults in it and nothing outside it. Scoping at the management group would grant access far beyond the requirement, and the role must be scoped to the target resources, not the virtual machines.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: Which tool can an administrator use to confirm what Azure role assignments a managed identity has across a subscription?
choices: The Microsoft Entra sign-in logs filtered to interactive sign-ins
The access control (IAM) check access feature for the identity
The provisioning logs filtered to the managed identity's object ID
The My Apps portal
questions.answer: The access control (IAM) check access feature for the identity
questions.explanation: Access control (IAM) lets you check access for a managed identity and list the Azure role assignments it holds at a scope. Interactive sign-in logs do not record managed identity sign-ins, and provisioning logs and My Apps are unrelated to Azure RBAC.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: A managed identity must be able to start and stop virtual machines in a resource group but must not delete them. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Assign Virtual Machine Contributor at the resource group so it can manage the machines
Assign Owner at the resource group and add a resource lock
Assign it an Azure custom role that has only the start and deallocate actions
Add the identity to a Microsoft Entra group with the Global Reader role
questions.answer: Assign it an Azure custom role that has only the start and deallocate actions
questions.explanation: An Azure custom role can include only the needed actions, which matches least privilege. Virtual Machine Contributor includes delete, and Microsoft Entra roles such as Global Reader do not grant Azure resource actions.

questions.stem: A company uses GitHub Actions to deploy to Azure and wants to stop storing client secrets in GitHub. Which approach should the identity administrator configure?
choices: A longer client secret expiry period combined with storing the secret as an encrypted GitHub secret
Password hash synchronization for the deployment account
A system-assigned managed identity on the GitHub runner organization
Workload identity federation on an app registration or user-assigned managed identity
questions.answer: Workload identity federation on an app registration or user-assigned managed identity
questions.explanation: Workload identity federation lets the external platform's own token be exchanged for a Microsoft Entra token, so no secret is stored in GitHub. A longer secret expiry keeps the secret problem and adds risk.

questions.stem: When a multitenant application from another company is consented to in your tenant, what is created in your tenant to represent it?
choices: A service principal (enterprise application)
An app registration owned by your tenant
A user-assigned managed identity
A guest user account
questions.answer: A service principal (enterprise application)
questions.explanation: The app registration (application object) lives in the publisher's home tenant, and consent creates a service principal, shown as an enterprise application, in each tenant that uses it. No guest or managed identity is created.

questions.stem: An app registration used by a scheduled job authenticates with a client secret. The security team asks for a stronger credential type that is still supported for apps running outside Azure. What should you recommend?
choices: A system-assigned managed identity
A certificate credential
A longer client secret
A Temporary Access Pass
questions.answer: A certificate credential
questions.explanation: Certificates are the recommended credential over client secrets for service principals because the private key is not sent and can be protected in a key store. A Temporary Access Pass is for users, and a system-assigned identity is unavailable outside Azure without Arc.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank has Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium licenses and wants to block a single-tenant service principal from signing in from outside approved IP ranges. Which feature should be used?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID Protection user risk policy
Application Proxy pre-authentication for the service principal
Conditional Access for workload identities
Self-service password reset
questions.answer: Conditional Access for workload identities
questions.explanation: Conditional Access for workload identities, licensed by Workload ID Premium, can block single-tenant service principals based on location or risk (managed identities are not covered). User risk policies target users, not service principals.

questions.stem: A security reviewer finds that a service principal used by a daemon app holds a client secret that expired yesterday. Which effect is MOST likely?
choices: The service principal is automatically converted to a managed identity
Users can no longer sign in to the app interactively with passwords
The app continues working for 90 days in a grace period
The app can no longer obtain tokens until a new credential is added
questions.answer: The app can no longer obtain tokens until a new credential is added
questions.explanation: An expired secret cannot be used in a token request, so the daemon fails until a new valid secret or certificate is added. There is no grace period and no automatic conversion to a managed identity.

questions.stem: Contoso is choosing between managed identity types. Which TWO statements describe a user-assigned managed identity?
choices: It can be attached to more than one Azure resource
It has a lifecycle independent of the resources that use it
It is removed automatically when its resource is deleted
Each resource can have only one of them
It requires a client secret that the administrator rotates
answers: It can be attached to more than one Azure resource
It has a lifecycle independent of the resources that use it
questions.explanation: A user-assigned identity is a standalone resource that can be shared and lives until deleted. Automatic removal with the resource describes a system-assigned identity, and neither type needs a secret.

questions.stem: The security team requires that a shared identity be granted Key Vault access before any virtual machine receives it. Put the steps in order to let several new virtual machines read secrets from Azure Key Vault.
items: Assign the Key Vault Secrets User role to the identity on the vault
Attach the identity to each virtual machine
From each virtual machine, request a token from the Instance Metadata Service by using the identity's client ID
Read the secret from Key Vault by using the token
questions.explanation: A user-assigned identity can be created first, and the requirement puts the role assignment before the identity is attached to the machines. Only an attached identity can get a token from the Instance Metadata Service, and the token is then used against Key Vault.

questions.stem: Match each workload to the identity that BEST fits it.

pairs.item: Azure virtual machine that calls Azure Storage
Build server in another cloud that deploys to Azure
pairs.match: Service principal with workload identity federation

pairs.item: Windows service on several on-premises domain-joined servers
Help desk technician who signs in interactively

questions.explanation: Azure-hosted workloads use managed identities, external workloads use a service principal (ideally federated), on-premises Windows services use a gMSA, and people use user accounts. A guest account is for external people, not workloads.

questions.topic: Accessing Azure resources with managed identities
questions.stem: Contoso's audit service uses a managed identity that may only read blob data from a single container. Which TWO actions should you take to follow least privilege?
choices: Assign the Storage Blob Data Reader role
Scope the role assignment to the container
Assign the Owner role on the storage account
Scope the role assignment to the subscription
Add the identity to the Global Reader role in Microsoft Entra ID
Store the storage account key in the app configuration
answers: Assign the Storage Blob Data Reader role
Scope the role assignment to the container
questions.explanation: The data reader role grants only blob read access, and scoping to the container limits it to that container. Global Reader is a Microsoft Entra role that grants no blob data access, and storing the account key defeats the purpose of a managed identity.

questions.topic: Enterprise app properties and tenant settings
questions.stem: Contoso added a SaaS app to Microsoft Entra ID and configured SSO. Only members of the Sales group should be able to get tokens for the app. Which application property must be set to Yes?
choices: Visible to users
Assignment required
Enabled for users to sign in
Owner approval required
questions.answer: Assignment required
questions.explanation: When assignment is required, only assigned users and groups can get tokens for the app, so assigning Sales enforces the restriction. Visible to users only controls whether the tile appears in My Apps.

questions.topic: Enterprise app properties and tenant settings
questions.stem: A company wants to keep an enterprise application working for assigned users but hide its tile from My Apps and the Microsoft 365 app launcher. Which property should you change?
choices: Assignment required
Enabled for users to sign in
Visible to users
Single sign-on mode
questions.answer: Visible to users
questions.explanation: Setting Visible to users to No hides the tile while leaving sign-in working. Turning off Enabled for users to sign in would stop everyone from signing in.

questions.topic: Enterprise app properties and tenant settings
questions.stem: An enterprise application is suspected of being misused. You must immediately stop all users from signing in to it while keeping its configuration for later investigation. What should you do?
choices: Delete the enterprise application
Set Visible to users to No
Remove the app's SAML signing certificate
Set Enabled for users to sign in to No
questions.answer: Set Enabled for users to sign in to No
questions.explanation: Disabling sign-in blocks token issuance for all users but keeps the app and its configuration. Deleting it loses the configuration, and hiding the tile does not block sign-in.

questions.topic: Enterprise app properties and tenant settings
questions.stem: An enterprise application has Assignment required set to No. Which statement is correct?
choices: Any user in the tenant can sign in to the app, but only assigned users see it in My Apps
No users can sign in to the app until an administrator assigns at least one user or group
Only guest users can sign in to the app
Users must request access through an access package and wait for approval before signing in
questions.answer: Any user in the tenant can sign in to the app, but only assigned users see it in My Apps
questions.explanation: With assignment not required, any user who reaches the app can get a token, while the My Apps tile shows only for assigned users. That is why assignment is usually required for apps that should be restricted.

questions.topic: Enterprise app properties and tenant settings
questions.stem: Fabrikam's security team wants one control, applied to every application in the tenant, that decides whether users can grant apps permissions to company data. Which setting should the team configure?
choices: Assignment required
User consent settings for applications
Visible to users
The SAML signing certificate
questions.answer: User consent settings for applications
questions.explanation: User consent settings apply to every app in the tenant and decide whether and how users can grant apps access to data. Assignment required, Visible to users and the signing certificate are set per application.

questions.stem: A help desk team must configure SAML SSO and user assignments for all SaaS enterprise applications, but must not manage Application Proxy. Which role should you assign, following least privilege?
choices: Application Administrator
Global Administrator
Cloud Application Administrator
Hybrid Identity Administrator
questions.answer: Cloud Application Administrator
questions.explanation: Cloud Application Administrator manages all aspects of app registrations and enterprise apps except Application Proxy. Application Administrator adds Application Proxy rights, which are not needed.

questions.stem: An administrator must publish on-premises web apps through Microsoft Entra Application Proxy and manage their enterprise application settings. Which role should be assigned, following least privilege?
choices: Cloud Application Administrator
Global Administrator
Security Administrator
Application Administrator
questions.answer: Application Administrator
questions.explanation: Application Administrator can manage enterprise apps including Application Proxy settings. Cloud Application Administrator has the same rights except Application Proxy, so it cannot complete the task.

questions.stem: A marketing manager must manage the configuration and user assignments of one specific enterprise application and no others. What should you do, following least privilege?
choices: Add the manager as an owner of that enterprise application
Assign the Cloud Application Administrator role at tenant scope
Assign the Application Administrator role at tenant scope to the manager
Assign the Global Reader role
questions.answer: Add the manager as an owner of that enterprise application
questions.explanation: An owner can manage the specific enterprise application they own without rights over other apps. The tenant-wide application roles would let the manager change every app, and Global Reader cannot make changes.

questions.stem: Users are not allowed to register applications in the tenant. A developer must be able to create app registrations without managing other users' apps. Which role should be assigned?
choices: Cloud Application Administrator
Application Developer
Application Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
questions.answer: Application Developer
questions.explanation: Application Developer lets a user create app registrations even when the tenant setting blocks users from registering apps, and makes them owner of what they create. The administrator roles grant control over all apps.

questions.stem: Contoso wants a group of operators to be able to manage only the user and group assignments of a set of enterprise apps, nothing else. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: The Cloud Application Administrator role at tenant scope
The User Administrator role, which manages users and their group memberships tenant-wide
A Microsoft Entra custom role with assignment permissions, scoped to those apps
An Azure custom role on the subscription
questions.answer: A Microsoft Entra custom role with assignment permissions, scoped to those apps
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra custom roles can grant specific enterprise application permissions and be scoped to individual applications. User Administrator manages users, not app assignments, and Azure custom roles control Azure resources, not Entra apps.

questions.stem: Adatum wants remote users to reach an on-premises intranet web app without a VPN and without opening inbound firewall ports. Which solution should you use?
choices: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
Password-based SSO in My Apps
Cross-tenant synchronization
Microsoft Entra Application Proxy
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra Application Proxy
questions.explanation: Application Proxy publishes on-premises web apps through connectors that make only outbound connections, so no inbound ports or VPN are needed. Connect Sync synchronizes identities and does not publish apps.

questions.stem: Where should you install the Microsoft Entra private network connector used by Application Proxy?
choices: On a Windows server on-premises that can reach the internal app
On a domain controller in a perimeter network with inbound HTTPS open
On each user's device
On the SaaS provider's web server that hosts the public endpoint
questions.answer: On a Windows server on-premises that can reach the internal app
questions.explanation: The connector runs on a Windows server inside the network that can reach the back-end app and connects outbound to the service. It does not need inbound ports, and it is not installed on user devices.

questions.stem: An on-premises app published through Application Proxy uses Integrated Windows Authentication. Users must get SSO after signing in to Microsoft Entra ID. What must you configure?
choices: Password hash synchronization so the connector can replay each user's password
Kerberos constrained delegation from the connector servers to the app
SAML token encryption on the app
A SCIM provisioning connector
questions.answer: Kerberos constrained delegation from the connector servers to the app
questions.explanation: For Integrated Windows Authentication apps, the connector uses Kerberos constrained delegation to get a Kerberos ticket for the user, which requires domain-joined connectors with delegation configured. Password hash sync and SCIM do not provide Kerberos SSO.

questions.stem: Contoso publishes an internal app with Application Proxy. Conditional Access policies must apply before any traffic reaches the internal app. Which pre-authentication method should be selected?
choices: Passthrough
Anonymous
Microsoft Entra ID
Basic
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explanation: With Microsoft Entra ID pre-authentication, users must sign in and satisfy Conditional Access before the connector forwards traffic. Passthrough sends requests to the app without Microsoft Entra authentication.

questions.stem: A company has a single Application Proxy connector serving a critical app and wants to avoid an outage if that server fails. What should you do?
choices: Open an inbound firewall port to the internal app as a fallback path for remote users
Create a second enterprise application for the same URL
Increase the token lifetime for the app
Install a second connector and place both in the same connector group
questions.answer: Install a second connector and place both in the same connector group
questions.explanation: Connectors in the same connector group share load and provide high availability, so a second connector removes the single point of failure. Opening inbound ports defeats the design of Application Proxy.

questions.stem: An on-premises app was built to trust identity values that a front-end access gateway inserts into each incoming request, and it has no support for SAML, OpenID Connect or Windows authentication. Which Application Proxy SSO method should you configure?
choices: Header-based single sign-on
Kerberos constrained delegation
Password-based single sign-on
Linked single sign-on
questions.answer: Header-based single sign-on
questions.explanation: Application Proxy can inject identity headers for apps that rely on header-based authentication. Kerberos constrained delegation is for Integrated Windows Authentication apps.

questions.stem: You are configuring SAML SSO for a gallery app. The vendor gives you the URL where Microsoft Entra ID must post the SAML response. In which setting do you enter it?
choices: Identifier (Entity ID) that uniquely names the app
Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL)
Sign-on URL
Relay state (where users land after sign-in)
questions.answer: Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL)
questions.explanation: The reply URL, also called the Assertion Consumer Service URL, is where Microsoft Entra ID sends the SAML response. The identifier uniquely names the app, and the sign-on URL starts service-provider-initiated sign-in.

questions.stem: A legacy web app has no support for SAML or OpenID Connect and uses its own sign-in form. Users want to sign in from My Apps without retyping credentials. Which SSO method should you use?
choices: SAML-based single sign-on
Header-based single sign-on through Application Proxy
Password-based single sign-on
Linked single sign-on
questions.answer: Password-based single sign-on
questions.explanation: Password-based SSO stores credentials and fills the app's sign-in form through the My Apps browser extension. Linked SSO only adds a link to the app and does not sign the user in.

questions.stem: Contoso wants accounts in a SaaS app to be created when users are assigned and disabled when users leave. The app supports SCIM 2.0. What should you configure?
choices: Password-based SSO
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
A My Apps collection
Automatic provisioning for the enterprise application
questions.answer: Automatic provisioning for the enterprise application
questions.explanation: Automatic user provisioning uses SCIM to create, update and deactivate accounts in the SaaS app based on assignments and attribute changes. SSO alone does not create or remove accounts, and Connect Sync syncs from on-premises Active Directory.

questions.stem: Provisioning to a SaaS app must include only users whose department attribute is Finance, even though a large group is assigned. What should you configure?
choices: A scoping filter on the provisioning attribute mappings
A Conditional Access policy for the app that targets the Finance department
An app collection in My Apps
A token lifetime policy that applies only to the Finance department's users
questions.answer: A scoping filter on the provisioning attribute mappings
questions.explanation: Scoping filters limit which users are provisioned based on attribute values. Conditional Access controls sign-in, not which accounts are created.

questions.stem: An administrator changed a user's attributes and needs to confirm right away that the change provisions correctly to the SaaS app without waiting for the next cycle. What should the administrator use?
choices: Restart the Microsoft Entra Connect Sync service
Provision on demand
Rotate the SAML signing certificate
Clear the provisioning logs
questions.answer: Provision on demand
questions.explanation: Provision on demand runs provisioning for a single user immediately and shows each step. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync does not handle app provisioning to SaaS apps.

questions.stem: Provisioning to a SaaS app has stopped, and the job shows it is in quarantine. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: More users are assigned to the application than the provisioning service allows per cycle
The application's Visible to users property is set to No
Most requests fail, for example because the admin credentials are invalid
The SAML signing certificate was renewed
questions.answer: Most requests fail, for example because the admin credentials are invalid
questions.explanation: The provisioning service quarantines a job when most calls fail, often because the target credentials are wrong or expired. The number of assigned users and the visibility setting do not cause quarantine.

questions.stem: The SAML signing certificate of a critical SaaS app expires in a few weeks. Which action keeps SSO working with the LEAST disruption?
choices: Delete the old certificate first and then create a new one
Switch the app to linked SSO until the vendor confirms it has imported a replacement certificate
Turn off assignment required during the change
Add a new certificate, share it with the vendor, then activate it before expiry
questions.answer: Add a new certificate, share it with the vendor, then activate it before expiry
questions.explanation: Adding a new certificate and coordinating with the vendor before activating it avoids a gap in SSO. Deleting the old certificate first would break sign-in immediately.

questions.stem: A SaaS app defines app roles named Viewer and Approver in its application manifest. Managers must receive the Approver role in the token. What should you do?
choices: Assign the managers' group to the enterprise application with the Approver role
Add the managers to the Application Administrator role
Create a Conditional Access policy that targets the app for the managers' security group
Add the managers as owners of the app registration so they can edit the app's roles
questions.answer: Assign the managers' group to the enterprise application with the Approver role
questions.explanation: Assigning a user or group to the enterprise application with a specific app role makes that role appear in the user's token roles claim. Directory roles and ownership do not set app roles in tokens.

questions.stem: Contoso wants to assign an enterprise application to a security group rather than to individual users. Which license requirement applies?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID Free is enough for group-based assignment
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher
Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium
Microsoft Entra ID Governance only
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher
questions.explanation: Group-based assignment to enterprise applications needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher; the Free edition supports only direct user assignment. Workload ID Premium is for workload identities.

questions.stem: An administrator assigns a parent group that contains several nested groups to an enterprise app. Members of the nested groups report they cannot access the app. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Nested groups must be mail-enabled to be assigned
Assignment required must be set to No for groups
Group-based app assignment does not include members of nested groups
The app must use password-based SSO for group assignment
questions.answer: Group-based app assignment does not include members of nested groups
questions.explanation: When a group is assigned to an application, only its direct members get access; members of nested groups do not. The fix is to assign the nested groups directly or flatten membership.

questions.stem: Where are the app roles that you assign to users and groups for an enterprise application originally defined?
choices: In the tenant's user consent settings
In a Conditional Access policy
In an Azure custom role definition
In the application's app registration
questions.answer: In the application's app registration
questions.explanation: App roles are defined on the application object (app registration) and then assigned to users, groups or service principals through the enterprise application. Azure custom roles control Azure resources, not app roles.

questions.stem: An application must call another API by using application permissions with no signed-in user. How is an app role of the API granted to the calling application?
choices: By assigning the app role to the calling app's service principal through admin consent
By adding the calling app's service principal to a security group that is assigned to the API
By setting Visible to users to Yes
By adding the calling app to a My Apps collection
questions.answer: By assigning the app role to the calling app's service principal through admin consent
questions.explanation: Application permissions are app roles of the API assigned to the client's service principal, which requires admin consent. Groups, visibility and collections do not grant API permissions.

questions.stem: Fabrikam wants users to consent only to apps from verified publishers that request low-impact permissions, while all other requests need an administrator. Which user consent setting should be selected?
choices: Do not allow user consent
Allow user consent for apps from verified publishers, for selected permissions
Allow user consent for all apps
Let users consent to any app that requests only delegated permissions from any publisher
questions.answer: Allow user consent for apps from verified publishers, for selected permissions
questions.explanation: This setting limits user consent to verified publishers and to permissions classified as low impact, and other requests need admin consent. Blocking all user consent is stricter than the requirement.

questions.stem: User consent is disabled in the tenant. Users must still be able to ask for access to new apps, and designated reviewers should approve or deny those requests. What should you enable?
choices: Self-service password reset
Risk-based step-up consent
The admin consent workflow
App collections in My Apps
questions.answer: The admin consent workflow
questions.explanation: The admin consent workflow lets users request consent, which designated reviewers can approve or deny. Risk-based step-up consent only escalates risky requests to admins and does not route ordinary requests.

questions.stem: An app requests Microsoft Graph application permissions. Which role can grant tenant-wide admin consent for these permissions, following least privilege?
choices: Cloud Application Administrator
Application Administrator
User Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
questions.answer: Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explanation: Granting Microsoft Graph application permissions (app roles) requires Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator. Cloud Application Administrator and Application Administrator can grant other consents but not Microsoft Graph app roles.

questions.stem: Which permission classification is used to decide which permissions users can consent to when user consent is limited to selected permissions?
choices: Low impact
Tenant critical
Admin restricted
Privileged
questions.answer: Low impact
questions.explanation: Administrators classify delegated permissions as low impact, and the user consent setting for selected permissions allows users to consent only to those. The other labels are not permission classifications in Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.stem: A security analyst finds an unknown app that users consented to and that has access to mailboxes. What should be done FIRST to stop the app from accessing data while investigating?
choices: Delete the users who consented
Disable sign-in for the app's enterprise application
Change the tenant's user consent setting only
Remove the app from all My Apps collections
questions.answer: Disable sign-in for the app's enterprise application
questions.explanation: Disabling sign-in for the enterprise application stops it from getting new tokens immediately while keeping its record for investigation; permissions can be reviewed and revoked next. Changing tenant consent settings only affects future consents.

questions.stem: Contoso wants users in the Finance department to see their finance apps grouped together on a separate tab in My Apps. What should you create?
choices: A connector group
An administrative unit
An app collection assigned to the Finance group
An access package catalog
questions.answer: An app collection assigned to the Finance group
questions.explanation: Collections group apps into tabs in My Apps and can be assigned to users or groups. Users still see only apps they are assigned to inside a collection.

questions.stem: An administrator adds an app to a My Apps collection assigned to all users, but some users still do not see the app. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Collections can contain only Microsoft 365 apps
Collections require Application Proxy
Collections show only apps that use SAML-based SSO
Those users are not assigned to the app itself
questions.answer: Those users are not assigned to the app itself
questions.explanation: A collection only organizes apps a user already has access to; users must also be assigned to the application to see it. Collections can contain any app the users are assigned to.

questions.stem: Users ask for a single place where they can launch all the enterprise apps assigned to them and request access to others. Which portal should you point them to?
choices: My Apps
Microsoft Entra admin center
Azure portal
Microsoft Defender portal
questions.answer: My Apps
questions.explanation: My Apps is the end-user portal for launching assigned apps, viewing collections and requesting access. The admin center and Azure portal are administrative tools.

questions.stem: A user configured password-based SSO for an app in My Apps but the credentials are not filled in automatically. What is the MOST likely missing component?
choices: The private network connector on the user's device
The My Apps Secure Sign-in Extension in the browser
A SCIM provisioning connector
A Kerberos ticket for the app
questions.answer: The My Apps Secure Sign-in Extension in the browser
questions.explanation: Password-based SSO relies on the My Apps browser extension to fill in stored credentials. The private network connector runs on servers for Application Proxy, not on user devices.

questions.stem: An administrator wants users to be able to group their own assigned apps into personal collections in My Apps. What should the administrator know?
choices: Only administrators can create collections
User-created collections replace all administrator collections for that user in My Apps
Users can create their own collections in My Apps in addition to admin-created ones
Each user can create personal collections only after an administrator approves an access review
questions.answer: Users can create their own collections in My Apps in addition to admin-created ones
questions.explanation: Users can build personal collections in My Apps, and these appear alongside any collections the administrator assigned. No access review or admin action is needed.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to publish an on-premises web app through Microsoft Entra Application Proxy.
items: Install the private network connector on an on-premises Windows server
Confirm the connector is active and in a connector group
Add an on-premises application with its internal and external URLs
Assign users or groups to the application and test access
questions.explanation: The connector must be installed and active before an app can be published to its group; then the app is added with its URLs and pre-authentication, and finally users are assigned and access is tested.

questions.stem: Match each administrative task to the least-privileged role or assignment that can perform it.

pairs.item: Configure SAML SSO for any SaaS enterprise app, but no Application Proxy
Publish an on-premises app with Application Proxy
Grant admin consent to Microsoft Graph application permissions
Manage one specific enterprise app only
Create app registrations when users cannot register apps

questions.explanation: Each task maps to the narrowest role that covers it. Global Administrator could perform them all but is never the least-privileged choice.

questions.stem: Contoso disables user consent but wants users to request access to new apps without filing a ticket. Which TWO actions should you take?
choices: Enable the admin consent workflow
Designate reviewers for consent requests
Set Assignment required to No on every app
Enable password-based SSO for every app
Assign all users the Cloud Application Administrator role
questions.explanation: The admin consent workflow sends requests to designated reviewers, who approve or deny them. Giving every user an application role would remove the control that disabled consent was meant to provide.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to set up automatic SCIM provisioning to a gallery SaaS app.
items: Add the gallery application as an enterprise application
Set the provisioning mode to Automatic
Enter the tenant URL and secret token as admin credentials and test the connection
Review the attribute mappings and scoping filters
Turn the provisioning status on and review the provisioning logs
questions.explanation: The app is added first, then automatic provisioning is selected so the admin credentials can be entered and tested; the mappings and scope are reviewed once the connection is saved, and only then is provisioning started and checked in the logs.
